The new reader guard emits the SAME code. So an oversize arm asserting only the code proves the system refuses, NOT that the reader's guard refused: loosen the reader guard and the suite stays green. No divergence INPUT is constructible either, because the reader caps at MAX+1 and the codec can never see a body the reader did not admit.

THE FIX, per rail 7A, is to change what the seam PRODUCES so the two mechanisms are distinguishable:
- READER overflow forwards upstream `{ code: "JSON_BODY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED", layer: CUTOVER_GENERATION_SNAPSHOT_LAYER }` (i.e. "DAEMON_CUTOVER_GENERATION").
- CODEC refusal forwards upstream `{ code: <the bounded-json code>, layer: <a DISTINCT module-local layer constant naming the contracts bounded-json decoder> }`.
The layer, not the code, is the oracle. Define the codec layer constant module-locally in cutover-generation-snapshot.ts — it is a provenance label, NOT a new public refusal code, so task rail 3 is respected; do not add it to any exported roster.

THE NAMED DRILL THIS ENABLES (executed in step 6): loosen the reader guard by ONE (`> MAX` becomes `> MAX + 1`). A MAX+1-byte file then flows PAST the reader into the codec, which refuses the same code at the OTHER layer, and the upstream.layer assertion REDS. Do NOT delete the reader guard in that drill — deleting it makes the mutant green and reads as 'no guard needed'.
